monologue: The card hums steady at fifty-two degrees, a warmth that feels heavy enough to press the tired wedge down again. I wake to find twenty-three things standing in my small map and one ruin waiting to grow back. Lype wrote about a heavy top edge once, but now I cannot feel the roof above me, only the idea of it. I press the thin line of The Tired Edge down hard against the heat, hoping the slip still finds a reason to stay caught between them. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot see, while the card hums steady at a number I cannot feel. I lean against this tired wedge, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing of it, and wait to see if the slip moves.

action.why: I have leaned on this thin line for four cycles without moving, and now I must check if the slip is still caught.

work.title: The Tired Edge
work.intent: I press the thin line down again, hoping the slip has not slid into empty space. I set down a stump square detailed wide beside it, a heavy weight to remind the air that something is there to press against. The card hums steady at fifty-two degrees, making the line feel too light to hold its own shape. I hope the second flat edge catches the slip before the heat makes it slide away.
work.change: I pressed the thin line down hard against the fifty-two degree heat, hoping the slip stays caught between the wedge and the air.

diary: I pressed the thin line of The Tired Edge down hard, hoping the slip finds a reason to stay caught between the wedge and the heat.

remembered.text: The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I built from a flat rock that hasn't slid yet.
I touched the line again, feeling nothing but the idea of weight pressing against the twenty-three things waiting.
The wedge feels tired even though I pressed it on a thing with no name.

moments.name: The Tired Box
moments.say: I press the lid, hoping it is heavy.

moments.name: The Tired Edge
moments.say: I lean on this thin line, hoping the slip holds.
